scan.summary: This is Evergreen Botanicals' state license to grow recreational marijuana indoors at 2210 Bailey Hill Road, with up to 10,000 sq ft of mature plant canopy. The current one-year term runs March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027. The license is the OLCC's own document, so there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is getting the renewal application and fee to the OLCC by February 10, 2027, and meeting the five conditions printed on it: tracking every item in CTS, making sure everyone who handles product holds a worker permit, keeping 90 days of video, reporting changes before they happen, and displaying the license where the public can see it.
scan.freshness_note: This is the current term, issued March 3, 2026. You don't need a newer copy until the next renewal is approved, which should be around March 3, 2027. The Authorized signature line on this copy is blank. It may just be a printed or electronic copy, but it's worth checking that the posted original is the signed one, or matches what the OLCC licensing portal shows.

conditions.title: The license covers only 2210 Bailey Hill Road and only Evergreen Botanicals, LLC. It cannot be transferred to another location or person.
conditions.evidence_expected: Proof that all production happens at the licensed address: a premises diagram on file with the OLCC that matches the actual layout, and no growing at any other site under this license.

conditions.title: Renew every year. The OLCC must receive the renewal application and fee at least 20 days before expiration (by February 10, 2027 for this term).
conditions.evidence_expected: The submitted renewal application and fee receipt, dated no later than February 10, 2027, plus the OLCC's confirmation that the application is complete.

conditions.title: Track every marijuana item at the premises in the Cannabis Tracking System (CTS).
conditions.evidence_expected: CTS records (plant tags, harvest lots, transfers, waste) that match physical inventory, and internal reconciliation records.

conditions.title: Every employee who handles marijuana items must hold a current OLCC marijuana worker permit.
conditions.evidence_expected: A staff roster with each person's worker permit number and expiration date, and copies of the permits. Worker permits are renewed every five years under OAR 845-025-5580.

conditions.title: Keep video surveillance at the premises that meets OAR 845-025-1450, and keep recordings for at least 90 days.
conditions.evidence_expected: Camera coverage map, recorder settings showing at least 90 days of storage, periodic checks that footage is retained, and system maintenance and outage logs.

conditions.title: Report any change in ownership, in the premises, or in the people with a financial interest to the OLCC before it takes effect.
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of change notices and OLCC approvals, each dated before the change. A current ownership and financial-interest list that matches OLCC records.

conditions.title: Display the license at the premises where the public can see it.
conditions.evidence_expected: The current-term license posted at the Bailey Hill premises. A dated photo of it posted is useful to keep.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on identity, dates, premises, tier, canopy and conditions. The page is clean and every item is read directly from page 1. The renewal date of 2027-02-10 is my own calculation: 20 days before March 2, 2027, where February 2027 has 28 days. Three things I'm less sure of. (1) The current wording of OAR 845-025-1190 appears to let a licensee who files on or before the expiration date keep operating, while OAR 845-025-1070 charges late-renewal fees if the OLCC receives the application less than 20 days before expiration. The license itself says 20 days, so treat February 10 as your real deadline. I did not confirm whether filing late also affects your right to keep operating under the current rule. (2) I did not check the current text of OAR 845-025-1450, so I am relying on the license's own statement of 90 days of video retention. (3) The Authorized signature line on this copy is blank, and I can't tell whether that is normal for an electronic copy. Permits have no gaps, so no gaps are listed.

OREGON LIQUOR AND CANNABIS COMMISSION
9079 SE McLoughlin Blvd, Portland, Oregon 97222
RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA PRODUCER LICENSE
License number: 020-1004763A8B2
Licensee: Evergreen Botanicals, LLC
Trade name: Evergreen Botanicals
Licensed premises: 2210 Bailey Hill Road, Eugene, Oregon 97405
License type: Producer — Tier II, Indoor
Canopy limit: 10,000 square feet mature plant canopy
Original issue date: March 3, 2022
Current term: March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027
Expiration date: March 2, 2027
This license is issued under ORS 475C and the rules of the Commission in OAR chapter 845, division 25, and
authorizes the licensee to produce marijuana at the licensed premises named above, subject to those rules and to the
conditions below.
Conditions of this license:
1. The license is valid only for the premises named above and is not transferable to any other location or person.
2. The license must be renewed annually. A renewal application and the renewal fee must be received by the
Commission no later than 20 days before the expiration date. A licensee that has submitted a complete renewal
application before that date may continue to operate until the Commission acts on it.
3. All marijuana items at the premises must be tracked in the Cannabis Tracking System, and every employee who
handles marijuana items must hold a current marijuana worker permit issued by the Commission.
4. Video surveillance meeting OAR 845-025-1450 must be maintained at the premises and recordings kept for at
least 90 days.
5. Any change in ownership, in the premises, or in the persons with a financial interest in the licensee must be
reported to the Commission before it takes effect.
This license must be displayed at the licensed premises where it can be seen by the public.
Issued by the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission
Date of issue for the current term: March 3, 2026
Authorized signature: ____________________ Licensing Director
